text: On the first day of the week, at early dawn, the women came to the tomb bringing the spices they had prepared.

versions.text: On the first day of the week, at early dawn, they came to the tomb bringing the spices they had prepared.
versions.explanation: For oral reading, the unidentified "they" at the start of a chapter is unclear; naming the women (implied by the feminine participle φέρουσαι and the previous context) helps listeners follow.

text: They found the stone rolled away from the tomb,
but when they went in, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
While they stood there bewildered, two men in dazzling clothes suddenly stood beside them.
The women were terrified and bowed their faces to the ground, but the men said to them: "Why do you look for the living among the dead?
He is not here; he has risen. Remember how he told you, while he was still in Galilee,
that the Son of Man must be handed over to sinful men, be crucified, and rise again on the third day."
Then they remembered his words.
And returning from the tomb, they reported all this to the Eleven and to all the rest.
It was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the other women with them who told this to the apostles.
But these words seemed to them like nonsense, and they did not believe the women.
Peter, however, got up and ran to the tomb. Stooping down, he saw only the linen cloths, and he went home, amazed at what had happened.
Now that same day two of them were walking to a village called Emmaus, about seven miles from Jerusalem,
and they were talking with each other about everything that had happened.
As they talked and discussed it, Jesus himself came near and walked along with them,
but their eyes were kept from recognizing him.
He said to them, "What is this you are debating with each other as you walk along?" They stopped, their faces downcast.
One of them, named Cleopas, answered him, "Are you the only visitor to Jerusalem who does not know what has happened there in these days?"
"What things?" he asked. They said to him: "About Jesus of Nazareth. He was a prophet, mighty in deed and word before God and all the people,
and how our chief priests and rulers handed him over to be sentenced to death, and crucified him.
But we had hoped that he was the one who would redeem Israel. And besides all this, it is now the third day since these things happened.
What is more, some of our women astounded us. They were at the tomb early this morning,
and when they did not find his body, they came back saying they had even seen a vision of angels who said he was alive.
Then some of our companions went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but him they did not see."
He said to them: "How foolish you are, and how slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken!
Did not the Christ have to suffer these things and then enter his glory?"
And beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, he explained to them what was said about himself in all the Scriptures.
As they came near the village where they were going, he acted as if he were going farther.
But they urged him strongly: "Stay with us, for it is nearly evening; the day is almost over." So he went in to stay with them.
When he was at the table with them, he took the bread, blessed it, broke it, and began to give it to them.

versions.text: When he was at the table with them, he took the bread, gave thanks, broke it, and began to give it to them.
versions.explanation: εὐλόγησεν means "blessed"; "gave thanks" renders εὐχαριστέω, a different verb. The blessing language should be preserved.

text: Then their eyes were opened and they recognized him—and he vanished from their sight.
They said to each other, "Were not our hearts burning within us while he talked with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?"
They got up that very hour and returned to Jerusalem, where they found the Eleven and those with them gathered together,
saying, "It is true! The Lord has risen and has appeared to Simon."
Then the two told what had happened on the road, and how he was made known to them in the breaking of the bread.
While they were still talking about this, Jesus himself stood among them.[^ Some manuscripts add: and said to them, "Peace be with you."]

versions.text: While they were still talking about this, Jesus himself stood among them and said to them, "Peace be with you."
versions.explanation: The clause "and said to them, 'Peace be with you'" is not present in the source text provided; it belongs to a variant reading. If retained, it should be marked in a footnote as found in some manuscripts rather than presented as part of the text.

versions.text: While they were still talking about this, Jesus himself stood among them.
versions.explanation: The removal of the greeting from the main text was correct, since the source text marks it as a variant. However, the variant is widely attested, and a brief textual footnote would inform the reader without disturbing the reading flow. The wording of the verse itself needs no change; "Jesus himself" for αὐτὸς is a natural clarification for oral reading, since the Greek pronoun would otherwise be ambiguous in English.

text: They were startled and terrified, thinking they were seeing a ghost.
He said to them: "Why are you troubled, and why do doubts rise in your hearts?
Look at my hands and my feet. It is I myself. Touch me and see; a ghost does not have flesh and bones, as you see that I have."
When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.
And while they still did not believe it for joy and were amazed, he asked them, "Do you have anything here to eat?"
They gave him a piece of broiled fish,
and he took it and ate it in their presence.
He said to them: "This is what I told you while I was still with you—that everything written about me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms must be fulfilled."
Then he opened their minds to understand the Scriptures.
He said to them: "This is what is written: the Christ will suffer and rise from the dead on the third day,
and repentance and forgiveness of sins will be preached in his name to all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.
You are witnesses of these things.
And behold, I am sending upon you what my Father has promised; but stay in the city until you have been clothed with power from on high."

versions.text: And behold, I am sending you what my Father has promised; but stay in the city until you have been clothed with power from on high."
versions.explanation: The Greek reads ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς, "upon you," which conveys the sending down of the promised Spirit rather than merely sending something to them.

text: Then he led them out as far as Bethany, and lifting up his hands, he blessed them.
While he was blessing them, he parted from them and was carried up into heaven.

versions.text: While he was blessing them, he left them and was taken up into heaven.
versions.explanation: διέστη ἀπʼ αὐτῶν means 'he was parted/separated from them'; 'he left them' can sound like abandonment in English and loses the passive, God-caused sense of the departure. 'Was carried up' also renders ἀνεφέρετο (imperfect passive) more vividly for oral reading. A footnote noting that some early manuscripts omit 'and was carried up into heaven' would be useful here.

text: And they worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy,
and they were continually in the temple, praising God.
